2. Material facts are that the opposite party-plaintiff-decree holder obtained a decree on 27-3-2001 in Civil Suit No. 619 of 1999 in the High Court of Kolkata against defendant Judgment-debtor herein petitioner for a sum of USD 30,091 equivalent to Rs 12,93,920 with interest and costs. Thereafter the decree holder under section 44A(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly as the Code) filed the certified copy of the said decree in the Court of 

 3. In execution case, the judgment-debtor by the applications dated 19-8-2004 and 23-8-2004 sought to dismiss the case as not maintainable and returned the case record to the Court of District Judge contending that the aforesaid foreign decree passed by the Kolkata High Court which is not the decree of reciprocating territory as described in section 44A(1) of the Code and the District Court means the only District Judge, so the joint District Judge has no jurisdiction to execute the said decree and as such the case record is required to be returned, which were rejected by the trial Court and affirmed in revision by the impugned order. 

 6. In revision, it is averred that the proper forum of execution of a foreign Judgment and decree of a reciprocating territory under section 44A(1) of the Code being the Court of District Judge and not in the Court of Joint District Judge. The aforesaid execution case No. 1 of 2004 cannot be proceeded with in the Court of Joint District Judge and can be proceeded with only in the Court of District Judge, under section 44A(1) of the Code. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party by filing Counter Affidavit opposes the Rule and submits that the certified copy of the foreign decree was field in the Court of District Judge, who by exercising its power under sections 38 and 39 of the Code transferred the execution case to the Court of Joint District Judge, for execution, who is empowered by law to execute such decree. Therefore, the Court below rightly rejected those applications which call for no interference by this Court. 

 10. Ongoing to materials on record it transpires that the decree holder filed a certified copy of the said foreign decree in the Court of District Judge, under section 44A(1) of the Code, upon which the instant execution was started. 

 "Where a certified copy of a decree of any of the superior Court of any reciprocating territory has been filed in a District Court, the decree may be executed in Bangladesh as if it had been passed by the District Court." 

 "20. (1) Save as otherwise provided by any enactment for the time being in force, an appeal from a decree or order of a District Judge or Additional District Judge shall lie to the High Court Division. (2) An appeal shall not lie to the High Court Division from a decree or order of an Additional District Judge in any case in which, if the decree or order has been made by the District Judge, an appeal would not lie to that Court." 

 "21. (1) Save as aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Joint District Judge shall lie-(a) To the District Judge where the value of the original suit in which or in any proceeding arising out of which the decree or order was made did not exceed five lakh taka. (b) To the High Court Division in any other case. 

 (2) Save as aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Senior Assistant Judge or an Assistant Judge shall lie to the District Judge, 

 16. Under section 18 of the Act the jurisdiction of a District Judge or a Joint District Judge extends (subject to provision of section 15 of the Code) to all original suits (for the time being) cognizable by civil Courts. Both the Courts have concurrent jurisdiction to take cognizance and try all original suits cognizable by Civil Courts: Under section 20 of the Act from a decree or an order of a District Judge or Additional District Judge an appeal shall lie to the High Court Division. Under section 21(1)(a) of the Act from a decree or order of a Joint District Judge an appeal shall lie to the District Judge where the value of the original suit in which or in any proceeding arising out of which the decree or order was made did not exceed Taka 5,00,000. On a reading of sections 20 and 21 of the Act it is apparent that the Court of the Joint District Judge is lower in grade in relation to the Court of the District Judge though concurrent jurisdiction has been given to both the Courts under section 18 of the Act. 

 21. Under section 2(4) of the Code a principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction of a District is called "District Court". Under section 44A(1) of the Code the certified copy of a decree of any of the superior Courts of any reciprocating territory is to be filed in a District Court for the purpose of executing the same. Therefore, we are to find out the meaning of "District Court" as used in section 44A(1) of the Code. In other words, could we regard the Court of the Joint District Judge having concurrent jurisdiction with the District Judge under section 18 of the Act as the "District Court" under section 44A(1) of the Code. We have considered sections 3 and 24 of the Code and sections 3, 10 and 21 of the Act and come to the conclusion the Court of the Joint District Judge is inferior in grade in relation to the Court of the District Judge. 

 24. The word "District Court" as used in section 44A(1) is primarily to be interpreted with reference to the definition of the "District Court" as given in section 2(4) of the Code. On consideration of the plain meaning of "Principal" as given in the Oxford Dictionary read with section 24 of the Code; and section 3(15) of the General Clauses Act, 1897 we are of the opinion that the "District Court" referred to in section 44A(1) of the Code means the Court of the District Judge under section 3(1) of the Act and no other Court though under section 18 of the Act concurrent jurisdiction had been given to the District Judge and the Joint District Judge in respect of all original suits cognizable by Civil Courts. Therefore, under section 44A(1) of the Code certified copy of the decree in question is to be filed only in the Court of the District Judge and in no other Court. 

 "38. A decree may be executed either by the Court which passed it, or by the Court to which it is sent for execution. 

 39. (1) The Court which passed a decree may, on the application of the decree-holder, sent it for execution to another Court— 

 (a) if the person against whom the decree is passed actually and voluntarily resides or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or 

 (b) if such person has no property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed the decree sufficient to satisfy such decree and has property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or 

 (c) if the decree directs the sale or delivery of immovable property situate outside the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed, it, or 

 (d) if the Court which passed the decree considers for any other reason, which it shall record in writing, that the decree should be executed by which other Court. 

 (2) The Court which passed a decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction. 

 26. In view of the provisions laid down in sections 2(4), 32, 15, 24, 38 and 39 of the Code, sections 3, 10, 18, 20 and 21 of the Act and section 3(15) of the General Clauses Act, 1897 the District Court mentioned in section 44A(1) of the Code means only the Court of the District Judge. In other words certified copy of the decree under section 44A(1) of the Code must be filed in the Court of District Judge. It is pertinent to point out that admittedly the decree-holder under section 44A(1) of the Code filed the certified copy in the Court of District Judge and ultimately it was transferred to Court of Joint District Judge for execution. After combined reading of the aforesaid provisions particularly sections 44A(1) and 39(2) of the Code, we are of the view that the joint District Judge has the jurisdiction to execute the foreign decree whose certified copy was filed in the Court of District Judge and subsequently transferred to him. Therefore, the Courts below after appreciating materials on record by rejecting the applications committed no error of law.
